_README: Classified divergences for ci/fixture_ab.sh - both engines against RVF's own
regression fixture, per assertion, in about 45 seconds.
Its own file because the fixture is not a release. The other baselines record
causes proven on real editions; these are proven on 58 files of deliberately
broken 2013 test data, and a cause from here transfers nowhere. Same contract
as the others: an unlisted divergence fails the gate, and a listed one that
stops diverging is reported so it can be removed.
WHAT THIS ARM IS FOR. The nightly A/B is the real measurement and costs 40
minutes against an 892MB release. This answers 'did my change move any
assertion' in 45 seconds, which is the question an engine change actually
raises. It has already earned it twice in one afternoon: it caught the jar
being stale (eight assertions still under-reporting because the binary
predated the anti-run fix), and it confirmed that fix against a LIVE MySQL
rather than against expectation files from 2023.
Measured 2026-09-10 with groups=release-type-validation:
122 assertions joined, 117 identical (95.9%), 5 divergent - all below.
MySQL 99 failures, DuckDB 99 failures.
WHY THE FIXTURE MUST BE REPACKED, not read in place: RF2 files are CRLF and
RVF's MySQL loader says so - `lines terminated by '\r\n' ignore 1 lines`. The
fixture in this repo is LF-only, so that statement reads each file as ONE
line, discards it, and loads 0 rows with no error: 90 empty tables and every
previous-dependent assertion passing over nothing. ci/fixture_ab.sh
normalises to CRLF when it packs, which makes the fixture a conformant
package. Before that normalisation this arm read 50.9% identical and every
MySQL number in it was meaningless.

directions.candidate-higher: DuckDB reports more failures than MySQL for an assertion
directions.incumbent-higher: MySQL reports more failures than DuckDB for an assertion

cause: The shared cause for all five, and it is the fixture's data, not either
engine's reading of an assertion.
sct2_Description_Snapshot-en_INT_20130731.txt has a 9-field header and
then 26 rows of 9 fields, ONE row of 10, and FOUR rows of 8. Five
malformed rows in one file, and every divergence in this arm is a
description assertion.
The two loaders disagree about them, which is not a defect in either:
MySQL's LOAD DATA pads a short row and truncates a long one, recording a
warning and keeping the row; DuckDB's materialiser refuses the strict
read - it logs `description_s: strict read refused` on this fixture - and
re-reads tolerantly. Two defensible answers to malformed input, and the
2-to-4 extra findings DuckDB reports follow from retaining them
differently.
This is baselined rather than chased because the input is wrong. A real
release is not ragged: the AU edition's description snapshot has 350 CRLF
line endings, no bare LF, and no ragged rows. Repairing the fixture would
retire all five entries at once, and that is the moveWhen.
evidence: DuckMaterialiser logs on this fixture: description_d, description_f, description_s strict read refused
